checks.why: Soft-min Hessian has the negative beta times gradient-covariance term. Gaussian integration by parts applies after X=C^(1/2)G, including singular C. Fixed-beta first and second derivative bounds justify differentiation. A and B are nonnegative quadratic-form averages, but their difference has no sign conclusion.

Integrating at fixed finite family before beta tends to infinity is legitimate. Deterministic endpoint error is at most 2 log K/beta as stated. Two-singleton-path near-tie calculation retains beta B and correctly detects the xi=0 endpoint derivative failure.

Each path and its finite minimum is xi sqrt(v)-Lipschitz in standard Gaussian coordinates. Gaussian Poincare covers Lipschitz nonsmooth functions. Cantelli yields the stated mean-median bound sqrt(Var), sharper than the elementary sqrt(2 Var) bound in my independent packet. Fixed xi, v_n=O(L_n), and L_n -> infinity suffice for normalized transfer.

Endpoint exponent convergence and log K_n/(beta_n L_n)->0 justify the integrated normalized reduction without pointwise response limits. The displayed simple-path counting bound is loose but sufficient; beta_n=N_n^2 meets the stated entropy condition when N_n and L_n diverge.

The proof explicitly leaves evaluation of the normalized signed interpolation response open. Discrete-to-continuum exponent conventions also require primary comparison evidence. Neither concentration nor finite interpolation evaluates lambda(xi) or d_gamma.
